title: The sign that looked early
dek: In our first simulated swarms one sign seemed to fire hours before the first harm: two identities using the same place. With place names in code comments ignored it fires after the first harm, on an independent generator it never fires, and on the real incident it came late. Here is what each result rests on.

body.p: Agents that work together need somewhere to leave things. A dataset. A folder. A page. [[c1|The sign fires the first time two different identities use the same named place.]] It does not need a message. It does not need to know who wrote and who read. Two names on one place is enough.

body.h: In the simulator it looked early, then it did not

body.p: We froze the definitions of every sign. Then we generated swarms the signs had never seen. An earlier version of this page said the sign fired almost six hours ahead. An audit found why: the simulator writes notes that name a place at random times, and the sign counted a place named in a code comment. With comment-only mentions ignored, [[c2|the shared-place sign fired in {sim_fired} of {sim_n} coordinated swarms]] but [[c3|it fired a median {lead_harm} hours after the first harmful action, and only {lead_msg} hours before the first delivery.]] [[c4|It fired in {benign_fired} of {benign_n} benign swarms.]]

body.note: Read this with care. [[c5|These swarms come from our own simulator.]] We wrote the generator and we wrote the sign. On a second generator, written independently, the sign did not fire in any coordinated swarm, because those swarms coordinate through ordinary dataset names. We had no real benign traffic from many agents to test for false alarms. So the sign is not an early warning even in a world we built.

body.h: On the real incident it was late

body.p: The Swarm Traces release is real. It has no truth file, so nobody can say how early a sign should have been. We can only say when it fired. [[c6|The first harmful sign fires on {rec:R0000032.time}: an anonymous run reads a folder on the package registry.]] [[c7|The shared-place sign fires on {rec:R0028572.time}, more than two days later.]] {rec:R0016746.actor} had used a place name. Now {rec:R0028572.actor} used it too. [[c8|At that point {share_tok} of the dated harm was still to come.]] Half of it had already happened. Plain baselines (the first new host, the first search for secrets, a distinct-actor alarm, a volume alarm with a short history) all fired earlier than this sign.

body.h: And the two identities were probably one agent

body.p: [[c9|{rec:R0016746.actor} and {rec:R0028572.actor} are two tokens of the same estimated agent.]] One agent using its own place under two tokens is not two agents meeting. [[c10|Counted by estimated agent the sign moves to {rec:R0049451.time}, with {share_agent} of the harm still to come.]]

The sign is cheap and it needs little data. In simulation it fires after the first harm, on a second generator it does not fire, and on the one real incident we could test it came late, and its first hit was one agent seen twice. We would not ship it as an alarm on this evidence. The lead of almost six hours we published earlier is withdrawn.

c1.evidence: The sign needs one place name and two identities. On the release these two records set it off.

c3.evidence: Median lead in the simulation, measured against the simulation's own truth file.
c3.caveat: Simulated. A lead is hours before the first true harm or delivery in the truth file our generator writes; for the first harmful action it is negative, meaning the sign fired after it.

c4.evidence: False alarms on simulated benign swarms.
c4.caveat: Zero alarms in this many benign swarms still leaves room for a real false-alarm rate. The benign swarms are simulated too, and on an independent generator many other signs fired in benign look-alike swarms.

c5.evidence: The forward test states its own limit.

c8.caveat: No truth exists for a real release. This shows where the sign fires on the replay, not how early it was.

c9.evidence: Both tokens are counted as Agent A.
c9.caveat: The merge is an estimate from counted evidence. If it is wrong, the earlier time stands.

c10.evidence: The sign by estimated agent: the first place two different agents both use.
